result.summary: FINDINGS at target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (branch feature/binary-config-serve-20260930). Reviewed src/store.ts (SQLite transactions, atomic invariants, error rollback, concurrent control mutations) plus call-site reachability in coordinator/security/overview/runtime/mcp. store.ts is byte-identical between baseline 5672ead and target, so this assesses pre-existing code. No CRITICAL/HIGH found: the transactional core (create/transition/claimDispatch/finish) is correctly wrapped and rolls back cleanly under injected failure. 3 LOW findings: (1) finish() re-arms a failed worker to 'ready' passing only completed_at, so the failure summary written at store.ts:294 persists and is surfaced by publicWorker/CLI as a stale error on an active worker; (2) cancelDispatches() (store.ts:246-250) is the only multi-row mutation without this.db.transaction and is never paired atomically with the terminal transition, so partial cancellation is possible; (3) create()'s request_id fingerprint hashes the config-resolved SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, so an identical retry after a config change is rejected, breaking the documented safe-retry contract. Tests: bun test core+lifecycle+token-idle = 57 pass / 0 fail / exit 0 on Bun 1.4.2; 13 local fake-provider probes under /tmp. Artifacts: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md and findings.json.
result.details:
SETUP. Disposable clone at /tmp/rev11/repo checked out detached at d428e0f (git rev-parse HEAD confirmed). /workspace/repo left clean on its assigned baseline 5672ead2a526e07fea9ed11e58b3725e42013527; no source changes, commits, pushes or merges. Bun 1.4.2 installed at /tmp/opencode/bun-linux-x64/bun (snapshot 1.3.14 cannot read lockfileVersion 2); bun.lock verified byte-identical after bun install --frozen-lockfile.

FINDING 1 (LOW, high confidence, reproduced) stale error after re-arm. src/store.ts:296-297 re-arms a worker that still has a queued dispatch with this.transition(id,'ready',{completed_at:null}); the failure summary written at :294 is not cleared because transition() merges fields over the stored worker (:146-152). Trigger: running worker with a queued follow-up, turn settles as {status:'failed'}. publicWorker() then reports state 'ready' with error '<previous failure>'; CLI prints ERROR <text>. Consumers are display-only (security.ts:146, cli/overview.ts:232, runtime.ts:94) so impact is observability. Why not caught: tests/lifecycle.test.ts:229-246 covers the re-arm only with status 'completed'; the sibling path queueMessage explicitly passes error:null (coordinator.ts:239-243).

FINDING 2 (LOW, high confidence for the gap / medium for impact) src/store.ts:246-250 cancelDispatches() loops saveDispatch() as N independent commits; every other multi-statement invariant wraps this.db.transaction (create :71, transition :158, claimDispatch :252, finish :278). The coordinator always calls cancelDispatches() then a separate transition() (coordinator.ts:411-418, :489-495, :775-783, :799-804, :894-905, :935-958, :968-975), so 'all dispatches cancelled AND worker terminal' is never one commit; the statements are synchronous with no await between, so this is a process-crash window, not a JS interleaving. Injected a throw on the 2nd saveDispatch and got ['cancelled','pending','pending']. A worker stranded in running/waiting with all dispatches cancelled falls to 'waiting' (coordinator.ts:536-539) until deadline_at trips coordinator.ts:452-455.

FINDING 3 (LOW, high confidence, reproduced) src/store.ts:72-74 fingerprints the resolved input; coordinator.ts:185-190 fills timeout_seconds from SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS when the caller omits it, so an operator setting is baked into the idempotency key and :81-82 rejects mismatches. Two Coordinator instances over one Store differing only in that default (3600->1800) rejected an identical retry. Not covered by lifecycle.test.ts:13-17 / core.test.ts:88-120, which retry under unchanged config.

VERIFIED CLEAN (so others do not re-derive): create() rolls back teams/tasks/workers/events fully after a failure injected after the inserts (probe p13); nested savepoint rollback correct for finish->transition->patch and message->queueMessage->transition, including the deliberate enqueue-then-throw at coordinator.ts:225-232 (p2); notify()'s queueMicrotask deferral means waiters see committed rows, and it also fires on rollback but only as a spurious wake with no lost wakeup (p1); cross-connection lost update is unreachable because patch() re-reads before writing and acquireProcessLock (runtime.ts:145) plus the documented single-owner model enforce one writer (p10); UNIQUE(team_id,request_id) permits unlimited NULL request_id rows as intended (p9); spawnSchema.parse normalises key order so fingerprint ordering is stable (p5); -wal/-shm are created at 0600 because chmodSync precedes PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL (p4); finish()'s duplicate-completion guard precedes any write (store.ts:279-285); transition()'s same-state short-circuit (:160) is intentional and asserted by core.test.ts:113-118.

LIMITATIONS. Full suite intentionally not run (whole-suite reviewer's job). Multi-process concurrent writers not exercised beyond one two-connection probe. Filesystem-permission and redaction surfaces only spot-checked. No real cloud/model/infra calls: all providers and the agent were local fakes; reviewer experiments live only under /tmp/rev11.

Plus 13 standalone probe scripts under /tmp/rev11/probe against :memory: stores or throwaway /tmp files using tests/helpers FakeProvider/FakeAgent (all exit 0); logs in /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/store-tests.log and store-probes.log. Full suite not run by design.
tests.summary: 57 passed / 0 failed, exit 0, on the store-relevant suites (core, lifecycle, token-idle). 13 targeted probes for transaction rollback, nested savepoints, cancelDispatch atomicity, request_id fingerprint stability, WAL permissions and stale-error reachability all executed successfully. No test failures encountered.

result.followup_reason: Three actionable LOW findings in src/store.ts: (1) finish() re-arm to 'ready' at store.ts:296-297 leaves the terminal failure summary set at store.ts:294, so publicWorker/CLI report a stale error on an active worker; (2) cancelDispatches() at store.ts:246-250 lacks the this.db.transaction wrapper used by every other multi-row invariant and is never committed atomically with the terminal transition, permitting partial cancellation; (3) the request_id fingerprint at store.ts:72-74 includes the config-resolved default timeout, so an identical retry after a config change is rejected and the documented safe-retry contract breaks. All three are localized, cheap to fix, and currently untested.
